subject: Quantitative Aptitude
description: Triangle properties, similar triangles, Pythagoras, angle sums, polygons

questions.stem: The sum of the interior angles of any triangle is:
questions.explanation: Sum of triangle interior angles = 180°, in Euclidean geometry. Any triangle (acute, right, obtuse, isoceles, equilateral, scalene) — same. For polygon with n sides: sum = (n−2) × 180°. Square = 360°. Pentagon = 540°. Hexagon = 720°.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: By PYTHAGORAS theorem, in a right triangle with legs 6 and 8, the hypotenuse is:
questions.explanation: Hypotenuse² = 6² + 8² = 36 + 64 = 100 → Hypotenuse = 10. (6, 8, 10) is the (3, 4, 5) Pythagorean triple scaled by 2. Common triples: (3,4,5), (5,12,13), (7,24,25), (8,15,17). Distractor 12 = sum 6+8 minus 2. Distractor 14 = 6+8. Distractor 11 ≈ √121 (just an estimate).
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: An equilateral triangle has each interior angle equal to:
questions.explanation: Equilateral triangle: all sides equal → all angles equal. 180° / 3 = 60°. Distractor 1 = 30° (half angle in 30-60-90 triangle). Distractor 3 = 90° (right angle). Distractor 4 = 120° (interior of regular hexagon).
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: The area of a triangle with base 12 and height 5 is:
questions.explanation: Area = (1/2) × base × height = (1/2) × 12 × 5 = 30. Distractor 60 forgets the half. Distractor 17 = base + height. Distractor 120 = doubles correct.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: If two triangles are SIMILAR and the ratio of their corresponding sides is 2:3, the ratio of their AREAS is:
questions.explanation: Similar figures: ratio of AREAS = (ratio of sides)² = (2/3)² = 4/9. Ratio of VOLUMES = (ratio of sides)³ = (2/3)³ = 8/27. Distractor 1 = side ratio (linear, not areal). Distractor 4 = volume ratio.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: The sum of interior angles of a regular hexagon is:
questions.explanation: Polygon interior-angle sum = (n − 2) × 180°. Hexagon n=6 → 4 × 180° = 720°. Each angle of REGULAR hexagon = 720/6 = 120°. Distractor 540 = pentagon. Distractor 360 = quadrilateral. Distractor 180 = triangle.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: An ANGLE INSCRIBED in a semicircle is always:
questions.explanation: Thales' theorem: any angle inscribed in a semicircle (subtending the diameter) is a right angle (90°). The vertex can lie anywhere on the arc; the angle stays 90°. A famous early geometric theorem (Thales of Miletus, ~600 BCE).
